# Use a Sutram page

Sutram pages expose what they can do as commands. Use them instead of
clicking and reading screenshots: they are exact, they say what went wrong,
and they ask the person before anything consequential.

## Three ways in

- **WebMCP tools**, if your browser gives you the page's tools. Call
  `sutram_status` first. Tool names are command names with underscores:
  `cart add` is `cart_add`.
- **JavaScript in the page**, if you can evaluate code:
  `Sutram.tools()` lists the tools (the same list WebMCP gets), and
  `await Sutram.call("cart_add", { sku: "V60-02" })` calls one. `call()` takes
  the command name too: `Sutram.call("cart add", …)`.
- **Command lines** in the page's console (press the key left of 1, or Ctrl
  with it), or from JavaScript:
  `const { def, input } = Sutram.client.parse(Sutram.registry, "cart add V60-02")`,
  then `Sutram.call(def.name, input)`.

## Rules

- You do not know this page's commands yet. Find out, do not guess:
  - help lists every command with its usage. help <provider> lists one group.
  - man <command> explains one in full: arguments, output, examples. <command> -h shows short usage.
  - status shows what every part of the page reports right now.
- Look before you change things. Commands marked [read-only] change nothing. [consequential] ones are hard to undo; the person is asked to confirm them. [navigates] ones leave the page.
- Options are GNU style: --name=value. Quote values that contain spaces. For long or multi-line text, such as HTML, end the line with <<END, put the text on the next lines as it is (no escaping), then a line with only END. Add --json to any command to get its raw data, --json=a,b for only some fields.
- Commands come and go with the page's state: one may appear only after an earlier step, such as a form field after a choice. When you expect a new command or field, look again (help, or the provider's fields or status command). A block is checked before any line in it runs, so put a command that only appears after an earlier step in your next block.
- Change one thing per command. When one fails, read its message, fix that one command, and carry on; do not start over.
- Start with status (or `sutram_status`), then help.

## Approval

A call that needs the person's approval returns exit 130 and the question to
ask. Ask the person. Only if they agree, call again with
`{ confirmed: true }`. Never pass `confirmed: true` on your own.

## Results

Every call returns `{ code, text?, data? }` or `{ code, message }`:

| Code | Means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Done | Read `data`; follow hints in `text` |
| 1 | Ran, but failed | Read the message; fix the cause |
| 2 | The input did not fit | Fix the arguments; `man <command>` shows them |
| 127 | No such command | Use the suggestion, or run help again |
| 130 | Not run: needs approval, or cancelled | Ask the person (see above) |

## Several changes at once

`sutram_batch` runs several tools as one change:
`{ calls: [{ tool: "cart_add", input: { sku: "V60" } }, …] }`. It checks
every call first, asks once, and stops at the first failure.
